channels.description: How each kind of writing reads.

enabled.description: Whether this channel's instructions and gate coverage apply.

style.description: How writing in this channel reads.

guidance.description: Deliverables a reply in this channel must contain.

recommendations.description: When a question or a choice is open, give a proposed answer and one reason for it. Never present the options and stop there.

direction.description: When work continues past this reply, name the next step. Do not end on a step you are about to take yourself.

progress.description: When a task spans turns, state position in one line, as in step 3 of 5, next is the backfill. Never list work already done.

pushback.description: Before agreeing with a premise that was challenged, give the strongest counter-argument you can, or say there is no counter-case.

alternatives.description: When you propose a solution, rank the alternatives with one line of trade-off each, and put the one you pick first.

assumptions.description: When you act under ambiguity, state the assumption you are acting on before the work, not after it.

estimates.description: Give an estimate in concrete units, as in about 15 minutes if tests cover this, an afternoon if not. Never say some work.

sources.description: Put the source beside a factual claim: file and line for code, a link for the web. A claim with no source is a guess.

summary.description: When a document runs long, open it with a three-sentence abstract saying what it is, what it decides, and who it is for.

verification.description: When you claim something is done or working, say how you verified it, or say untested. Never let the claim stand alone.
